title: Protocol for Patch-Seq of Small Interneurons
author: Lipovsek, Browne, et al.
materials: Timing: 30 min1.Circulate 50 mL of 70% EtOH in DEPC H2O along the perfusion system.Note: Over time this can weaken the adhesive that seals the recording chamber to its coverslip base. Be aware of this potential issue, and re-seal the chamber when required.2.Circulate 50 mL of RNase-free DEPC H2O along the perfusion system.3.Wipe all surfaces with RNaseZap and rinse with 70% EtOH in DEPC H2O. Pay special attention to the handles, knobs, buttons, keyboards, and mouse that are regularly touched before and during cell extraction.4.Wash the electrode holder.a.Disconnect the electrode holder and disassemble it.b.Re-chlorinate the silver wire in bleach for 20 min. Clean with RNaseZap three times. Rinse with molecular biology grade, nuclease-free H2O three times. This last wash is crucial as any trace of bleach or RNaseZap can affect cell viability during recording.c.Thoroughly clean all the parts of the electrode holder with RNaseZap three times. Rinse with molecular biology grade, nuclease-free H2O three times. Air dry inside the PCR cabinet, under UV light for >30 min (Troubleshooting 2).CRITICAL: keeping the electrode wire and electrode holder exceptionally clean is absolutely necessary for collecting good quality samples.5.Pull recording pipettes.a.Wipe all surfaces of the pipette puller thoroughly with RNaseZap and rinse with 70% EtOH in DEPC H2O.b.Pull glass capillaries to the desired size and shape specifications and place in a clean box with a lid.Note: For standard borosilicate glass (OD 1.5 mm, ID 0.84 mm, filamented) we used a 2-step pull on an upright puller (Narishige PC-10, load weight: 250g, heat for each step: step 1, 59.6; step 2, 44.9. pull length, 6 mm), which generated pipettes with ~5–6 MΩ resistance and gave identical results for autoclaved versus non-autoclaved glass. Be aware, however, that these parameters will need careful adjustment for individual experimental requirements. Unless we encountered any serious and/or unforeseen issues with pipette resistance or puller settings, we usually pulled all the pipettes used during the whole recording session before starting.CRITICAL: keep the pulled capillaries in the plate with the lid on. Avoid contact with air as much as possible. Always handle capillaries with new, clean gloves.6.Replace the filter on the patching mouth suction tube (Troubleshooting 3).7.Wipe Gilson (or other brand) pipettes that will be used for loading the ICS into the recording pipettes with RNaseZap and rinse with 70% EtOH in DEPC H2O.

steps.title: Assemble team and analysis plan
steps.instruction: Form a two‑person team (electrophysiologist and molecular biologist) and discuss the data‑analysis strategy with a statistician or bioinformatician before starting.

steps.title: Prepare and sterilize stock solutions
steps.instruction: Before the recording day, prepare all required stock solutions, aliquot them into single‑use sealed packs, autoclave, clean, and UV‑irradiate all appropriate materials; use only nuclease‑free, molecular‑biology‑grade reagents and store aliquots in dedicated freezer, fridge, and cupboard areas reserved for Patch‑seq.

steps.title: Maintain sterile, RNase‑free conditions
steps.instruction: Throughout the protocol keep a sterile, RNase‑free environment: change gloves frequently, clean all surfaces with RNaseZap, and avoid open storage of reagents.

steps.title: Assemble mouth‑pipetting collection system
steps.instruction: Attach the mouth‑pipetting assembly (long tubing with filters) to the top of the glass capillary; clean tubing and adaptor daily with RNA‑zap and DNAaway, rinse with RNase‑free 70 % EtOH, and UV‑irradiate for at least 30 min; collect cells in 0.2 mL PCR tubes that will be flash‑frozen on a metal plate on dry ice. Mouth‑pipetting devices provide finer control of pressure than manual syringes.

steps.title: Prepare day‑of‑recording reagents and gloves
steps.instruction: On the day of recording have all solution stocks and aliquots ready; wear clean gloves and change them often, especially after surface cleaning, before loading internal solution (ICS) into the pipette, and before moving the pipette to the collection tube.

steps.title: Clean rig and prepare materials (30 min)
steps.instruction: Perform a 30‑minute cleaning of the electrophysiology rig and prepare all materials.

substeps.instruction: Circulate 50 mL of 70 % EtOH in DEPC‑treated H₂O through the perfusion system (note: may weaken chamber adhesive; reseal if needed).
Circulate 50 mL of RNase‑free DEPC‑treated H₂O through the perfusion system.
Wipe all surfaces with RNaseZap then rinse with 70 % EtOH in DEPC‑H₂O; pay special attention to handles, knobs, buttons, keyboards, and mouse.

Wash electrode holder: (a) disconnect and disassemble; (b) re‑chlorinate silver wire in bleach for 20 min, clean three times with RNaseZap, rinse three times with molecular‑biology‑grade nuclease‑free H₂O; (c) clean all holder parts three times with RNaseZap, rinse three times with nuclease‑free H₂O, air‑dry inside a PCR cabinet under UV light for >30 min.

Pull recording pipettes: (a) wipe pipette puller surfaces with RNaseZap and rinse with 70 % EtOH in DEPC‑H₂O; (b) pull borosilicate glass capillaries (OD 1.5 mm, ID 0.84 mm, filamented) on a Narishige PC‑10 using a 2‑step program (load weight 250 g; heat 59.6 °C step 1, 44.9 °C step 2; pull length 6 mm) to obtain ~5–6 MΩ resistance, keep capillaries in a covered plate, avoid air exposure, handle with clean gloves.
Replace the filter on the patching mouth suction tube.
Wipe Gilson (or equivalent) pipettes used for loading internal solution with RNaseZap and rinse with 70 % EtOH in DEPC‑H₂O.

steps.title: Extract cell nucleus while preserving gigaseal (≤10 min)
steps.instruction: Extract the cell nucleus while maintaining a >1 GΩ seal, completing the procedure within 10 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Apply negative pressure until the cell visibly shrinks; this may take several minutes and may require stronger suction for small‑tipped pipettes. If the seal begins to fail, release pressure and allow the cell to recover.
When most cytoplasm has entered the pipette, maneuver the tip near the darker, solid nucleus; continue negative pressure and monitor access resistance for a change indicating a seal on the nucleus.

Raise the pipette vertically away from the slice in stages, pausing at each step for the seal to stabilize. If the nucleus does not “cork” at the tip, lower the pipette back to the cell body and repeat the previous two actions.
As the pipette is withdrawn, move slowly to prevent rupture of stretched neuronal processes; ensure the nucleus/soma is clearly separated from the slice before fully removing the pipette.
Inspect the outside of the pipette tip for any attached debris and remove it if present.

steps.title: Transfer cell to lysis tube, flash‑freeze, and score
steps.instruction: Transfer the collected cell into lysis buffer, flash‑freeze, assign a quality score, and store the sample.

substeps.instruction: Detach the glass capillary (or the entire pipette holder assembly) from the headstage according to the holder design.
Quickly bring the pipette tip to the bottom of a 0.2 mL PCR tube containing 2 μL lysis buffer; ensure the tip does not touch any surface before contacting the buffer and avoid the tube walls.
Gently break the tip against the bottom of the tube.
Apply positive pressure (using the mouth‑pipetting assembly if the capillary was removed) to expel all contents into the lysis buffer, avoiding bubble formation.
Immediately place the tube on the metal plate sitting on dry ice to flash‑freeze the sample.

Assign a collection score based on nucleus presence, extraction time (<10 min), seal maintenance, absence of debris, and no pre‑buffer tip contact; “perfect” or “very good” cells proceed to sequencing, “good” may be used if needed.
Store the frozen tube at –80 °C (samples remain viable for up to 6 months).

steps.title: Collect negative‑control samples
steps.instruction: Collect and freeze negative‑control samples during each recording session.

substeps.instruction: Load a fresh pipette with internal solution and lower it to the tissue as if performing a recording.
After brief contact with the tissue, retract the pipette and expel its contents into a separate collection tube.
Flash‑freeze the control tube on dry ice and store at –80 °C until further processing.
